questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Easy access through the Erasmus program - lots of institutional help setting up the exchange. Interest in Italian culture.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: A little bit difficult online, but very helpful employees at the mobility office in Milan.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Email-correspondance with employees at the mobility office.

questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Facebook group.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Getting to see other parts of the town is great. More integration in the local youth community.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Online application to subjects. A little difficulty in planning due to very late publication of schedules (the weekend before start of term). Not taking courses from the same programme led to uncertainty of schedule feasibility. Also difficulty in registration due to teachers having manually to add me to the courses in myAriel.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Email contact with the mobility office.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: In the end, it all worked out.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Take it easy. It will all work out, but maybe a little slower than expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very interesting courses.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Good level. Interesting subjects and nice professors.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: 4 courses exclusively with lectures. 1 course with practical elements. Addressing professors with last name and title. Written closed book exams with pen and paper. Thus a little more "traditional" than in Copenhagen.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Applied entomology, Low environmental impact techniques and methodologies for the protection of plants, Microbial biotechnology, Plant-environment interactions, Ethical thinking and making hard choices.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Low environmental impact techniques and methodologies for the protection of plants; super qualified teacher with very good English, very small class (4 persons) with good opportunities to ask questions, practical components very different and interesting.

questions.answer: Do not know.

questions.answer: Do not know any.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Lake como, Venezia, Verona, Bologna. Go out of the city!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Mostly easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be polite and expect comfortable silence. Italians are better at that than Danes.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The male gaze was more prominent. More unwanted attention when going out at night or when walking alone during the day.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Sitting outside having time to do nothing. Waiting in line at the supermarket having time to chat to other people. Eating gelato and looking at happy dogs in the park.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: It takes time, but all the practicalities will come to order. The exams are different but the teachers forgiving and wanting you to succeed, the classmates are nice and very polite and helpful if you make contact.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Write emails to the student office if you are unsure about anything. They are very helpful.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Being in Italy in general.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Everything before. Getting an apartment and getting the schedule set up.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
